newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD hails French left-wing poll success.
newsitem.headline: German SPD hails French left-wing poll success.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Monday hailed the left-wing victory in the first round of France's parliamentary elections and said it showed voters had taken a stand against neo-liberal policies.
"The election is encouraging for Germany's Social Democrats (SPD)," SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine told journalists before an SPD conference on reforms for Europe.
"It shows that economic and financial policies which raise unemployment through restrictive budgets and social spending cuts are condemned to failure," he said.
Lafontaine said such policies had been rejected by British voters in their general election earlier this month and the French electorate was now doing the same.

The SPD hopes to emulate the successes of France's left wing, which won a 4.5-point lead over the unpopular government coalition parties, when it faces Chancellor Helmut Kohl in general elections next year.
Rudolf Scharping, SPD parliamentary leader, sent a congratulatory letter to Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin.
"You, dear Lionel, have given social democracy in France...a profile and hope through your personality, policies and dedication," Scharping wrote.

Scharping said the first-round result showed that people in Europe wanted policies which took seriously their desire for jobs and training as well as their wish for equality, social security and protection of personal freedom.
"I wish you, dear Lionel...success for the second round -- sucess against neo-liberalism and against new nationalism."

Juergen Trittin, spokesman of the Greens party, said the result was a clear protest against neo-liberal policies and hoped the "red-green alliance" of Socialists, Greens and Communists would win the second round as well.
German media commentators called the poll results a sensational slap at President Jacques Chirac but warned voters could still turn to the right in the second round.
The strongest commentary came from West German Radio in Cologne, which called the result a debacle for Chirac and "more than just a warning."

"The real loser is Jacques Chirac, who has managed to provoke such a defeat just two years after taking office," it said. "It is questionable if a president can govern effectively on such a narrow popular basis.

The Westfaelische Nachrichten newspaper said: "French voters have let off some steam. The government parties ... could not communicate two things to the voters -- the purpose of a vote right now and whether they were competent to solve the problems France faces."
The Frankfurter Rundschau daily commented: "Jacques Chirac has miscalculated and his surprise attack has gone wrong."
